title: StructLens: A Structural Lens for Language Models via Maximum Spanning Trees
abstract: arXiv:2603.03328v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Language exhibits inherent structures, a property that explains both language acquisition and language change. Given this characteristic, we expect language models to manifest their own internal structures as well. While interpretability research has investigated how models compute representations mechanistically through attention patterns and Sparse AutoEncoders, the organization of the resulting representations is overlooked. To address this gap, we introduce StructLens, a framework to analyze representations through a holistic structural view. StructLens constructs maximum spanning trees based on the semantic representations in residual streams, inspired by tree representation in dependency parsing, and provides summaries of token relationships in representation space. translated_title: StructLens：基于最大生成树的语言模型结构透镜
translated_abstract: 语言具有内在的结构，这一特性既解释了语言的习得，也解释了语言的演变。基于这一特性，我们期望语言模型同样能展现出其自身的内部结构。尽管可解释性研究已经通过注意力模式和稀疏自编码器探究了模型如何以机制化的方式计算表示，但由此产生的表示的组织方式却一直被忽视。为填补这一空白，我们提出了StructLens，一个通过整体结构性视角来分析表示的框架。StructLens受依存句法分析中树形表示的启发，基于残差流中的语义表示构建最大生成树，从而在表示空间中提供词元间关系的摘要。我们分析了连续的词元在表示空间中是否也彼此邻近，发现中间层表现出最强的局部跨度组织特性。
tldr: 提出StructLens框架，受依存句法树启发，通过在残差流语义表示上构建最大生成树来揭示语言模型表示的整体内部结构，并发现中间层具有最强的局部跨度组织特性。
en_tdlr: We propose StructLens, a framework inspired by dependency-parsing trees that constructs maximum spanning trees over residual-stream semantic representations to reveal the holistic internal structure of language model representations, finding that middle layers exhibit the strongest local-span organization.
